Scaling up Nutrition Fund (SUN) är en gemensam finansieringsmekanism som stöds av DFID, Irish Aid och Sida och Zambias regering för att stödja den nationella First 1000 Most Critical Days Programme - ett nutritionsprogram som syftar till att förebygga kortväxthet hos barn genom att fokusera på den kritiska tiden från befruktning upp till 2 års ålder som är den viktigaste tidpunkten för intervention.

The Scaling up Nutrition Fund (SUN) is a joint funding mechanism supported by DFID, Irish Aid and Sida and the Government of Zambia to support the National First 1000 Most Critical Days Program - a nutritional program aimed at preventing stunting in children by focusing on the critical period from conception to 2 years of age which is the most important time of intervention.

To examine Programme Effects, the evaluation conducted a household survey of 2,392 households in two evaluation districts and compared with control districts. From these the evaluation found: Increases in:-Early breastfeeding initiation (10 percentage points) and knowledge (9 percentage points)- Consumption of iron rich or fortified foods (2 5 percentage points)- Likelihood of receiving a nutritionally acceptable diet (5 percentage points) Decreases in: - Likelihood of having had diarrhea in the past 2 weeks (13 percentage points)
Impact: Estimates suggest that stunting fell by 4 percentage points more in treatment districts (33% to 28%) than comparison districts (24% to 23%) although the difference is not statistically significant. Of note was the start of nutrition programmes targeting comparison districts which may have affected results. Also worth considering was the greater positive effects on stunting in younger children who were likely to have been exposed to a full package of interventions for longer (Brudevold-Newman A. et al 2018).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
